ui.indexMetaTitle: Unbit error help: what each message means
ui.indexMetaDescription: Short explanations of the messages Unbit shows when a BitLocker drive won’t open, with what to try for each.
ui.indexSub: What each message means and what to do about it.
ui.stillStuckText: In Unbit, open the gear menu and choose Copy Error Report, then include it when you ask for help. It contains no passwords, drive names or file paths.

steps: Check the password for typos and make sure Caps Lock is off.
Use the 48-digit recovery key instead. It’s in the Microsoft account that encrypted the drive, on a printout, or in a .txt file saved when BitLocker was turned on. Every drive has its own.
If a code you saved in Unbit stopped working, choose Enter New Code and type the current one.
On a Windows PC, open the drive’s BitLocker settings (right-click the drive and choose Manage BitLocker).
Add a password and save a recovery key for the drive. Unbit can’t use the TPM, smart cards or startup key files.
Plug the drive into the Mac again and open it with the new password or recovery key.
Choose another partition in the drive list. A drive can have several partitions, and only one of them may be encrypted.
If macOS can already read the partition, open it in Finder – it isn’t encrypted with BitLocker.
Open the drive on a Windows PC and copy its files to another disk.
To use the drive on a Mac later, turn BitLocker off and encrypt it again with a current Windows version.
Plug the drive into a Windows PC and run chkdsk, or repair-bde with the recovery key.
If Windows is still encrypting or decrypting the drive, let it finish first.
Don’t format the drive. Copy what you can to another disk first.
Check the cable and try another USB port, directly on the Mac rather than through a hub.
Plug the drive in again and choose Refresh Drive List in Unbit.
If it keeps failing, the drive may be failing. Copy its files on a Windows PC while you still can.
Open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access, turn on Unbit, then return to the app.
In Unbit’s gear menu choose Set Up Read Access… and approve once with your Mac password.
If the setting doesn’t seem to apply, quit Unbit and open it again.
Wait a moment and choose Try Again.
Plug the drive in again, then choose Refresh Drive List in Unbit.
If it keeps happening, restart the Mac and try once more.

invalid-input.title: The code isn’t valid
invalid-input.meaning: The recovery key must have 48 digits (8 groups of 6). Check that it's typed correctly.

wrong-password.title: Wrong password
wrong-password.meaning: Wrong password. Check for typos and Caps Lock and try again, or unlock with the recovery key instead.

wrong-recovery-key.title: Wrong recovery key
wrong-recovery-key.meaning: Wrong recovery key. Check all 48 digits – every drive has its own recovery key.

saved-password-stale.title: The saved password no longer works
saved-password-stale.meaning: The saved password no longer matches this drive. Choose Enter New Code and type the current password.

saved-recovery-key-stale.title: The saved recovery key no longer works
saved-recovery-key-stale.meaning: The saved recovery key no longer matches this drive. Choose Enter New Code and type the current recovery key.

no-password-protector.title: The drive has no password
no-password-protector.meaning: The drive isn't protected with a password. Use the recovery key instead.

no-recovery-protector.title: The drive has no recovery key
no-recovery-protector.meaning: The drive has no recovery key. Use the password instead.

no-supported-protector.title: Only a startup key, smart card or TPM
no-supported-protector.meaning: This drive can only be unlocked with a startup key file, a smart card or the TPM, which Unbit can't use. On a Windows PC, add a password or recovery key to the drive (Manage BitLocker), then try again.

not-bit-locker.title: This isn’t a BitLocker partition
not-bit-locker.meaning: This partition isn't BitLocker-encrypted. Choose another partition, or open the drive in Finder if it isn't encrypted.

not-bit-locker-readable.title: macOS can already read this partition
not-bit-locker-readable.meaning: macOS can already read this partition, so it isn't BitLocker-encrypted. Open it in Finder, or choose another partition.

unsupported-version.title: Unsupported BitLocker version
unsupported-version.meaning: Unbit opens drives encrypted with Windows 7 or later. This drive uses an older BitLocker version (Windows Vista).

unsupported-encryption.title: Unsupported encryption method
unsupported-encryption.meaning: This drive uses an encryption method Unbit doesn't support. Open it on a Windows PC instead.

damaged-metadata.title: The BitLocker information is damaged
damaged-metadata.meaning: The BitLocker information on this drive is damaged or incomplete. Check the drive on a Windows PC (for example with chkdsk or repair-bde) and try again.

conversion-in-progress.title: Windows is still encrypting or decrypting the drive
conversion-in-progress.meaning: The drive is being encrypted or decrypted by Windows right now. Let Windows finish first, then try again.

drive-removed.title: The drive was removed
drive-removed.meaning: The drive was removed. Plug it in again to open it.

damaged-key.title: No usable volume key
damaged-key.meaning: This drive has no usable volume key, so it can't be opened. It may be damaged or only partly encrypted – check it on a Windows PC.

drive-stopped-responding.title: The drive stopped responding
drive-stopped-responding.meaning: The drive stopped responding while it was being read. Check the cable and port, plug the drive in again, and try again.

read-failed.title: Couldn’t read from the drive
read-failed.meaning: Couldn't read from the drive. Check the cable and port, plug the drive in again, and try again.

attach-timed-out.title: macOS took too long to attach the drive
attach-timed-out.meaning: macOS took too long to attach the drive. Wait a moment and try again. If it keeps happening, plug the drive in again.

admin-prompt-timed-out.title: The administrator prompt timed out
admin-prompt-timed-out.meaning: The administrator prompt timed out. Try again and approve with your Mac password.

helper-timed-out.title: The read helper didn’t respond
helper-timed-out.meaning: The read helper didn't respond. Choose Set Up Read Access in the gear menu and try again.

timed-out.title: An operation timed out
timed-out.meaning: A step took longer than expected and was stopped, so nothing was changed on the drive.

admin-access-failed.title: Couldn’t get read access to the drive
admin-access-failed.meaning: Unbit couldn't get read access to the drive. Try again and approve with your Mac password, or choose Set Up Read Access in the gear menu.

no-access.title: macOS denied access to the drive
no-access.meaning: macOS denied access to the drive. Give “Unbit” Full Disk Access in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access, and try again.

other.title: Something went wrong
other.meaning: Unbit hit a problem it has no specific message for. The drive is opened read-only, so nothing on it was changed.
